text:
Situation: Lorazepam injection has been on FDA's shortage list since 2018-05-03 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 17 units of 2 mg/mL, 1 mL cartridges (3.4 days) and 30 units of 2 mg/mL, 10 mL SDV (4.4 days). Corvale General holds 99 units of 2 mg/mL, 1 mL (14.6 days) and 83 units of another 2 mg/mL, 1 mL lot (12.9 days). Oral tablets are well stocked at both sites.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the lorazepam injection shortage on 2018-05-03; status is Current as of 2026-10-21. The product labeler for our 2 mg/mL, 1 mL cartridges (NDC 00409198530) is Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262). FDA inspection 976095 at that plant ended 2016-06-08, classified OAI, 694 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 443 days before the posting. A later inspection 1064827 ended 2018-08-15, also classified OAI, 104 days after the posting.

Our position: The rule‑ranked transfer of 4 units from Corvale General to Corvale East is the preferred operational step. It raises East's 1 mL cartridge supply from 3.4 to 4 days while General retains approximately 14 days. Alternate concentration products from Hikma and Hospira are pharmacist‑verified and FDA‑listed Current but require dose and volume recalculation by the treating team. Civica supply is not on the FDA shortage list and its manufacturing site is unidentified.

Recommended actions:
1. Execute transfer of 4 units of lorazepam 2 mg/mL, 1 mL cartridges from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires approval by Pharmacy Director and a controlled‑substance transfer record (Schedule III‑V).
2. Evaluate Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 2 mg/mL lorazepam as an alternate source — requires pharmacist verification of dose and volume; previously approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2025-12-01.
3. Evaluate Hospira, Inc. 2 mg/mL lorazepam as an alternate source — requires pharmacist verification of dose and volume; previously approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2026-05-04.
4. Defer Civica, Inc. purchase pending identification of its manufacturing site and FDA shortage listing — requires buyer action if pursued.

Not recommended: Initiating any clinical dosing changes or protocol modifications; those are decisions for the treating clinicians and the P&T committee.
